problem:
The matrix $S$ is given below. Let ${s}_{1}$, ${s}_{2}$,  ${s}_{3}$ and ${s}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $S.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{s}_{1},{s}_{2},{s}_{3}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(S).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${s}_{4}={x}_{1}{s}_{1}+{x}_{2}{s}_{2}+{x}_{3}{s}_{3}.$ 

$$
S=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -5 & 5 \\ -2 & -1 & 10 & -1 \\ -1 & -2 & 5 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding a Basis of the Column Space of a Matrix

feedback.problem:
The matrix $C$ is given below. Let ${c}_{1}$, ${c}_{2}$,  ${c}_{3}$, and ${c}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $C.$ Determine if $B=\text{{}{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(C).$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$, where ${c}_{4}={x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}.$

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -4 & -3 & -8 \\ 3 & -4 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $C$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -4 & -3 & -8 \\ 3 & -4 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -12 \\ 3 & -4 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -12 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-\frac{1}{4}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(C)$ is ${{c}_{1},{c}_{2}},$ that is to say,

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -4 \\ -4\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Now, since the $4$th column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express ${c}_{4}$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -8 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{c}_{4}}={{(4)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{c}_{1}}+{{(3)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -4 \\ -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{c}_{2}}.
$$

This gives us ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=4\cdot 3=12.$
